# Server TypeScript migration (Phase 3)

Goal: convert every first-party .js file under server/ and index.js to TypeScript, one batch (directory) at a time. The vendored code in server/libs and all files under test/ stay as they are.

## Rules (apply to every batch)
1. At the end of every batch `npm run build:server` must report 0 "error TS" and `npm test` must show 356 passing, 0 failing. Never end a session with a red build.
2. Do not edit, skip or delete any test. Do not change files outside the batch unless a type error in the batch cannot be fixed otherwise; list any such change in the Log below.
3. Runtime behaviour must not change. Do not fix bugs. When types expose a bug, keep the behaviour, add a `NOTE:` comment at that line and add one line to the Bugs section below.
4. No `any`, no `@ts-ignore`, no `@ts-nocheck`, no `@ts-expect-error`. Use `unknown` and narrow it. Every type assertion (`as`) needs a one-line comment.
5. Module style (copied from Phase 1 and 2): local modules use `import X = require('./X')` and `export = X`, so existing require() callers, tests and sinon stubs keep working. Third-party packages with a default export use `import x from 'pkg'`.
6. Shared types live next to the data they describe (see server/providers/types.ts). Add a types.ts in the directory when two or more files share a type.
7. Convert with `git mv X.js X.ts` so history is kept. Keep JSDoc descriptions and drop JSDoc type annotations that the signature now carries.
8. At the end of each batch: update the Progress table, commit with the message `phase3 batch N: <directory>`, and stop.

## Progress
| Batch | Directory | Files | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | server/utils (all subfolders) | 46 | done |
| 2 | server/objects (all subfolders) | 18 | done |
| 3 | server/models | 25 | todo |
| 4 | server/auth and server/routers | 6 | done |
| 5 | server/managers | 18 | todo |
| 6 | server/scanner | 13 | todo |
| 7 | server/controllers (remaining 22) | 22 | todo |
| 8 | server/migrations | 15 | todo |
| 9 | server top-level files (Logger, Database, Auth, SocketAuthority, Watcher, Server) and index.js | 7 | todo |
| 10 | Packaging: package.json scripts, Dockerfile and anything else that references a .js entry point | 0 | todo |

Already done in Phase 2: server/finders, server/providers, server/controllers/SearchController.

## Bugs found (not fixed)
Each has a `NOTE:` comment at the line.
- server/utils/generators/opmlGenerator.ts: reads `podcast.itunesPageUrl` but the Podcast model field is `itunesPageURL`, so the OPML outline never gets an `htmlUrl`.
- server/utils/podcastUtils.ts `extractImage`: xml2js puts `<image>` in an array, so `channel.image.url` is always undefined and the RSS `<image><url>` is never used (always falls back to `itunes:image`).
- server/utils/podcastUtils.ts `extractEpisodeData`: the second `media:content` find does not require a url, so an audio `media:content` without a url makes `enclosure.url.trim()` throw.
- server/utils/scandir.ts `groupFileItemsIntoLibraryItemDirs`: a media file in the folder root is stored as a string group; if a directory has the same name, `.push` is called on that string and throws (2 places).
- server/utils/parsers/parseFullName.ts: `fixCase !== 'undefined'` compares with the string 'undefined' instead of using typeof, so that part of the check is always true.
- server/utils/parsers/parseFullName.ts `fixParsedNameCase`: the suffix check indexes `namePartLabels[j]` (word index) instead of `namePartLabels[i]` (label index).
- server/utils/comicBookExtractors.ts `CbzComicBookExtractor.open`: `getBuffer()` can return null, which is passed to `Archive.open` unchecked (the class is not used by `createComicBookExtractor` at the moment).
- server/utils/migrations/dbMigration.ts `handleOldLibraries`: maps `oldDbIdMap.libraries[library.oldLibraryId]`, but the Library model has no `oldLibraryId` (it was just written to `extraData`), so the key is "undefined" and old library ids in users' `librariesAccessible` are mapped to undefined and dropped.
- server/objects/files/LibraryFile.ts `setDataFromPath`: `getFileTimestampsWithIno` returns `false` when stat fails; the file is then created with `ino` undefined and no size/timestamps, and no error is reported.
- server/auth/TokenManager.ts `rotateTokensForSession`: when the conditional update hits 0 rows and the session row has been deleted in the meantime, `findOne` returns null and `updatedSession.refreshToken` throws.
- server/auth/OidcAuthStrategy.ts `verifyCallback`: when no user matches and auto-register is off, `user.isActive` is read on null and throws a TypeError, so the intended 'User not active or not found' error is never thrown (the login still fails, the log shows the TypeError).
- server/routers/ApiRouter.ts `getUserListeningStatsHelpers`: reads `s.lastUpdate`, but PlaybackSession has no `lastUpdate` (it is `updatedAt`), so `items[id].lastUpdate` is always undefined.

## Log
### Batch 1: server/utils (46 files, all converted, none skipped)
- New type files: `server/utils/types.ts` (shared utils types, `declare global` for the `global.*` values used in utils, and typed views of untyped vendored libs/models), `server/utils/parsers/types.ts`, `server/utils/queries/types.ts`, and `server/utils/ssrf-req-filter.d.ts` (ssrf-req-filter has no types; tsconfig excludes `*.d.ts`, so it is pulled in with a `/// <reference>` from `server/utils/types.ts`).
- devDependencies added (rule 10): `@types/express`, `@types/xml2js`, `@types/uuid`. They were already in node_modules as extraneous packages; `npm install` also pruned the other extraneous ones locally (`@types/passport`, `@types/cookie-parser`, `@types/express-session`, `@types/passport-strategy` ...), so later batches must add those to devDependencies when they need them.
- No files outside server/utils were changed (apart from package.json/package-lock.json and this file). No tests were changed.
- Module style: every module now ends in `export = <object/class/function>`. Modules that used `module.exports.x = ...` export one object literal with the same keys; checked that no utils module is in a require cycle, so assembling the export object at the end is safe. Internal `this.x()` / `module.exports.x()` calls go through that object, so sinon stubs on exports keep working. Compared `Object.keys`/`typeof` of every compiled module against HEAD: identical, except `parseFullName` is now a `function` declaration (needed for overloads) instead of an arrow function, so it has a `prototype`.
- Typed views for untyped JS (each a single commented `as` where the module is required): `FsExtra` for libs/fsExtra (its fs API is built at runtime), `ArchiverFactory` for libs/archiver, `SortInstance` for libs/fastSort, the fuse.js constructor in podcastUtils, ffprobe in prober, libarchive in comicBookExtractors.
- `TypedDatabase` (utils/types.ts): the JS models override `Model.init` with a different signature, so TypeScript rejects their static query methods (`findAll`, `count`, ...). Files that query cast `require('../../Database')` to `TypedDatabase` (same object; model getters still read lazily). It also types `sequelize` as set and `libraryFilterData`. Batch 3 (models) should make this unnecessary.
- Model associations (`book.libraryItem`, `series.bookSeries`, `mediaProgress.mediaItem`, ...) and JSON columns (`user.permissions`, `user.extraData`, `playbackSession.mediaMetadata`) are not declared on the JS models; the queries describe the loaded rows locally and cast once per query result. Sequelize's types are stricter than what it accepts at runtime (arrays of where options, `limit: null`, `[literal]` order items, a single nested include object, `distinct` on findAll, `limit` on count); those option objects use `QueryFindOptions` or are cast at the call with a comment.
- Behaviour-neutral code changes made for typing: `new Date() - n` became `new Date().valueOf() - n` (same coercion); a few repeated reads were pulled into a commented local (`permissions`, `mediaMetadata`, `models`); `getMediaGroupQuery` in libraryItemsBookFilters writes properties through a `mediaWhereHash` alias of the same object; `libraryFilters.getFilterData` replaces its sets with arrays through a typed alias of the same object; zipHelpers no longer requires express at runtime (it was only used for a JSDoc type); dbMigration no longer destructures the unused `QueryInterface` value from sequelize.
- JSDoc in not yet converted JS files that points at typedefs which moved (`import('../utils/fileUtils').FilePathItem`, `import('../utils/podcastUtils').RssPodcast*`, `import('./parseEbookMetadata').EBookFileScanData`) now resolves to `any` in those JS files; point them at `server/utils/types.ts`, `podcastUtils.ts` or `parsers/types.ts` when those files are converted.
- Incremental tsc crash: changing `server/utils/types.ts` (its `declare global` block) makes `tsc` crash with `Debug Failure. False expression` in `getSpecifierForModuleSymbol` while re-emitting signatures of JS files. A clean build works; fix with `rm dist-server/.tsbuildinfo`.
- Result: `npm run build:server` reports 0 `error TS`; `npm test` 356 passing, 0 failing.

### Batch 1 fixes (after independent review)
- abmetadataGenerator: restored the original `validated.series?.length` truthiness check (the batch had changed it to `Array.isArray(...) && ...length`); `series` is now typed `unknown[]` instead of using an `as`.
- Class fields declared without an initialiser in comicBookExtractors, utils/index (ValidationError, NotFoundError), rateLimiterFactory and longTimeout compiled to `field;` lines that created own properties set to undefined. They are now `declare` fields (rule 12) and compile to nothing, as in the JavaScript.
- Tried `"useDefineForClassFields": false` in tsconfig.server.json first and reverted it: it changed the compiled output of 21 files, including about 10 JS files that are not converted yet (ApiCacheManager, Database, Logger, TokenManager, MigrationManager, BinaryManager, User, DeviceInfo, ServerSettings, BookScanner), where real field initialisers move into the constructor body after parameter defaults. ApiCacheManager's `new LRUCache(this.defaultCacheOptions)` default then reads undefined and throws (348 passing, 1 failing).

### Batch 2 and 4: server/objects, server/auth, server/routers (24 files, all converted, none skipped)
- New type files: `server/objects/types.ts` (`FileMetadataJSON`, `AudioChapter`, `TaskString`, and `DateAndTime`, a typed view of the minified vendored libs/dateAndTime used by objects and ApiRouter) and `server/auth/types.ts` (`declare global`: `Express.User` extends the User model so `req.user` is typed, and `var RouterBasePath`; `PassportDone`, `JwtPayload`).
- devDependencies added (rule 10): `@types/passport` (passport.use/unuse and `req.user`), `@types/express-session` (`req.session` in OidcAuthStrategy).
- No files outside the batch were changed (apart from package.json/package-lock.json and this file). No tests were changed.
- Class fields: every field the JS assigned in the constructor or later (none were JS class fields) is a `declare` field (rule 12), so the classes compile to the same constructor bodies. The JS static field initialisers (`DeviceInfo.stringFields`, `ServerSettings.patchableSettingsKeys`, `TokenManager.TokenSecret`) stay normal static fields. `Task.failedAt` and `TrackProgressMonitor.currentTrackProgress`, set outside the constructor, are declared too.
- Fields the JS JSDoc typed as non-null but initialised to null (`AudioFile.metadata`/`metaTags`, `LibraryFile.metadata`, `EBookFile.metadata`, `PodcastEpisodeDownload.rssPodcastEpisode`/`libraryItem`/`url`) keep the non-null type with a commented `null as unknown as T` in the constructor; other null-initialised fields are typed `T | null`.
- Inputs of the constructors (stored JSON) are typed as the toJSON shape (`AudioFileData`, `LibraryFileData`, `NotificationData`, `PlaybackSessionData`, `ServerSettingsData` = `Partial<toJSON> & { storeCoverWithBook?, storeMetadataWithBook? }`, ...). `FileMetadata.toJSON` and `LibraryFile.toJSON` cast their result to the non-null shape the JS models expect (`LibraryFileObject` in models/LibraryItem).
- `global.ServerSettings` (declared in utils/types.ts from `ServerSettings['toJSON']`) is now fully typed.
- ApiRouter: the JS controllers type `req` as their own `RequestWithUser`, which express's `RequestHandler` does not accept, so `this.router` is typed `ApiRouterApp` (express app whose get/post/patch/delete take handlers with open parameters) with one commented cast at `express()`. The route lines are unchanged.
- `TypedDatabase` casts (as in batch 1) in TokenManager and ApiRouter. TokenManager also types the session rows as `SessionRow` (the JS Session model does not declare `refreshToken`); ApiRouter adds `getPlaybackSessions(where): Promise<PlaybackSession[]>` to its Database view (it returns false only before Database.init).
- Compared the compiled output of all 24 files with the JS compiled at 7f280c67 (comments stripped, printed with the TypeScript printer): AudioTrack and TrackProgressMonitor are identical, LocalAuthStrategy identical apart from quote style. All other differences are listed here:
  - Module style: `const { a } = require('x')` / `require('x').a` became `import x = require('x')` plus `const { a } = x` / `const a = x.a` after the imports (still destructured at module load, now after the other requires of the file; none of the destructured modules is in a require cycle with the file that destructures it, so they are fully loaded either way). Typed views are `const fs = fsExtra`, `const date = dateAndTime`, `const Database = DatabaseModule` (same objects).
  - OidcAuthStrategy: `const { Request, Response } = require('express')` (only used for JSDoc; both values were undefined) became `import type`, so this module no longer requires express at runtime. `axios` is a default import (`axios_1.default.get`, the same axios object; rule 5).
  - Local aliases of the same object, so dynamic keys type check (`this[key]` / `payload[key]` read and written through `self` / `values` / `newValues` / `existingValues` / `jsonValues` / `other`): FileMetadata `update`, `setData`; AudioMetaTags `toJSON` (`for (const key in this)` became `for (const key in self)`), `updateData`, `isEqual`; AudioFile `updateFromScan`, `mimeType` (`AudioMimeType[format]` became `mimeTypes[format]`); DeviceInfo `construct`, `toJSON`, `update`; Notification `update`; EmailSettings `update`; ServerSettings `update`.
  - OidcAuthStrategy: `req.query.x` became `query.x` with `const query = req.query` at the start of `generatePkce` and `getAuthorizationUrl` (before the try; `req.query` is a plain property); `req.session[sessionKey]` became `session[sessionKey]` with `const session = req.session`; `client.issuer.end_session_endpoint` (read twice) became `issuer.end_session_endpoint` with `const issuer = client.issuer`.
  - ApiRouter `getUserListeningStatsHelpers`: `listeningSessions.forEach(...)` became `sessionsForStats.forEach(...)` with `const sessionsForStats = listeningSessions`.
  - Casts on expressions (`(await findOne(...)) as SessionRow`, `(session.updatedAt || session.startedAt) as number | null`, `(this.timeListening as number) += ...`) only add parentheses in the output.
- Non-null assertions (`!`, each with a comment): `FileMetadata.filenameNoExt`, OidcAuthStrategy `handleMobileRedirect` (`openIdAuthSession.get(state)!`, `has(state)` is checked just before).
- Result: `npm run build:server` reports 0 `error TS`; `npm test` 356 passing, 0 failing.

## Extra rules
9. If a file cannot be typed cleanly without changing behaviour, first use the smallest possible `as` with a one-line comment and a line in the Bugs section. If that still fails, leave the file as .js, list it under Skipped with the reason, and move on.
10. You may add missing @types packages to devDependencies in package.json (for example express, passport, cookie-parser). Mention them in the Log.
11. Add the types in the same edit as the rename: `git mv`, then edit the file before running the build, because a bare rename can crash incremental tsc.
12. Declare class fields that the JavaScript did not initialise with `declare` (for example `declare timeout: NodeJS.Timeout`), so they compile to nothing whatever the tsconfig says. Fields the JavaScript did initialise stay as normal fields.

## Known deviations to clean up at the end
- The Phase 2 finders and providers (server/finders, server/providers) have the same class field issue: fields declared without an initialiser compile to `field;` lines (already present at 9c4185a0, for example `baseUrl;` in Audnexus and OpenLibrary). Mark them `declare` (rule 12).

## Skipped files
(none yet; batches 1, 2 and 4 skipped nothing)

## Rules added after the type quality audit (2026-10-09)

These rules apply from batch 3 onward. Where they conflict with rule 4 or rule 9, these rules win. Phase 2 and batches 1 to 4 were done under the earlier rules.

13. Batch 3 is split in two.
    - Batch 3a converts server/models. The models must declare their JSON columns (permissions, extraData, mediaMetadata, libraryFiles) and their associations (for example book.libraryItem, series.bookSeries), and must type size, mtime and ctime as they really are at runtime. Commit: `phase3 batch 3a: models`.
    - Batch 3b starts only after 3a is green and committed. It removes TypedDatabase, ApiDatabase, PatchModels, QueryFindOptions and every `as unknown as LibraryItem['media']` cast, using the real Sequelize types instead. This means editing files converted in earlier batches, with no behaviour change. Batch 3b is done only when `grep -rn "TypedDatabase" server` and `grep -rn "QueryFindOptions" server` find nothing. Commit: `phase3 batch 3b: remove model workarounds`.

14. Tag every new cast with its reason. Write `// cast(a): <why>` directly above the cast, where the letter is one of:
    - a: untyped or vendored library
    - b: Sequelize or Express typing limitation
    - c: a real mismatch in the original JavaScript. A cast tagged c must also have a NOTE comment and an entry under Bugs.
    - d: other
    This replaces the plain one-line comment for new casts. Existing casts are not retagged now.

15. Banned shortcuts. Do not use:
    - index signatures on domain types (allowed only for real dictionaries)
    - function types with `never` parameters
    - `null as unknown as T`. If the JavaScript assigns null or checks for null, declare the field `T | null` and handle null where it is used, without changing behaviour. If the JavaScript never initialised the field, use `declare x: T` (rule 12).
    - casting req.query or req.body to all-string shapes. Use `string | string[] | undefined`, or a small narrowing helper that keeps the same behaviour.
    If a file cannot be done without one of these, leave it as .js and list it under Skipped files with the reason.

16. Narrow with type guards, not with `as`. A parameter type must not be wider than the JSDoc it replaces (for example, no `unknown` where the JSDoc said `boolean`).

17. In every batch Log entry, report the count of `as`, `as unknown as` and non-null `!`, and the number of casts per tag (a, b, c, d). If any single kind of cast appears more than 10 times in a batch, stop and report it, because a shared type is probably missing.

18. For batch 7 (controllers): once controllers are TypeScript, type the request with its user as an extension of the Express Request and remove ApiRouterApp, so that the router can be a normal express.Router.

### Added to "Known deviations to clean up at the end" (from the audit)

- The 8 uses of `null as unknown as T` in batches 1 to 4 (find them with `grep -rn "null as unknown as" server --include=*.ts`), including OidcAuthStrategy.ts verifyCallback, where the cast hides the user.isActive bug listed under Bugs.
- ApiRouter.ts: RouteHandler is typed with `never` parameters, so handler signatures are not checked against what Express passes.
- FilteredLibraryItem has an index signature `[key: string]: unknown`.
- Casts of req.query to all-string shapes.
- About 450 casts in Phase 2 and batches 1 to 4 have no reason tag.

### Log
- 2026-10-09: Type quality audit finished (a4-context/phase3-evidence/audit/4-type-audit.md). Rules 13 to 18 added.

## Extra rules
9. If a file cannot be typed cleanly without changing behaviour, first use the smallest possible `as` with a one-line comment and a line in the Bugs section. If that still fails, leave the file as .js, list it under Skipped with the reason, and move on.
10. You may add missing @types packages to devDependencies in package.json (for example express, passport, cookie-parser). Mention them in the Log.
11. Add the types in the same edit as the rename: `git mv`, then edit the file before running the build, because a bare rename can crash incremental tsc.
12. Declare class fields that the JavaScript did not initialise with `declare` (for example `declare timeout: NodeJS.Timeout`), so they compile to nothing whatever the tsconfig says. Fields the JavaScript did initialise stay as normal fields.

## Rules added after the type quality audit (2026-10-09)

These rules apply from batch 3 onward. Where they conflict with rule 4 or rule 9, these rules win. Phase 2 and batches 1 to 4 were done under the earlier rules.

13. Batch 3 is split in two.
    - Batch 3a converts server/models. The models must declare their JSON columns (permissions, extraData, mediaMetadata, libraryFiles) and their associations (for example book.libraryItem, series.bookSeries), and must type size, mtime and ctime as they really are at runtime. Commit: `phase3 batch 3a: models`.
    - Batch 3b starts only after 3a is green and committed. It removes TypedDatabase, ApiDatabase, PatchModels, QueryFindOptions and every `as unknown as LibraryItem['media']` cast, using the real Sequelize types instead. This means editing files converted in earlier batches, with no behaviour change. Batch 3b is done only when `grep -rn "TypedDatabase" server` and `grep -rn "QueryFindOptions" server` find nothing. Commit: `phase3 batch 3b: remove model workarounds`.

14. Tag every new cast with its reason. Write `// cast(a): <why>` directly above the cast, where the letter is one of:
    - a: untyped or vendored library
    - b: Sequelize or Express typing limitation
    - c: a real mismatch in the original JavaScript. A cast tagged c must also have a NOTE comment and an entry under Bugs.
    - d: other
    This replaces the plain one-line comment for new casts. Existing casts are not retagged now.

15. Banned shortcuts. Do not use:
    - index signatures on domain types (allowed only for real dictionaries)
    - function types with `never` parameters
    - `null as unknown as T`. If the JavaScript assigns null or checks for null, declare the field `T | null` and handle null where it is used, without changing behaviour. If the JavaScript never initialised the field, use `declare x: T` (rule 12).
    - casting req.query or req.body to all-string shapes. Use `string | string[] | undefined`, or a small narrowing helper that keeps the same behaviour.
    If a file cannot be done without one of these, leave it as .js and list it under Skipped files with the reason.

16. Narrow with type guards, not with `as`. A parameter type must not be wider than the JSDoc it replaces (for example, no `unknown` where the JSDoc said `boolean`).

17. In every batch Log entry, report the count of `as`, `as unknown as` and non-null `!`, and the number of casts per tag (a, b, c, d). If any single kind of cast appears more than 10 times in a batch, stop and report it, because a shared type is probably missing.

18. For batch 7 (controllers): once controllers are TypeScript, type the request with its user as an extension of the Express Request and remove ApiRouterApp, so that the router can be a normal express.Router.

import type * as fsPromises from 'fs/promises'
import type * as fsSync from 'fs'
type ServerSettingsModel = import('../objects/settings/ServerSettings')
import type { Model, ModelStatic, Sequelize } from 'sequelize'

/**
 * Methods the vendored fs-extra (server/libs/fsExtra) adds on top of node fs (only the ones used)
 */
interface FsExtraMethods {
  copy(src: string, dest: string, options?: { overwrite?: boolean }): Promise<void>
  move(src: string, dest: string, options?: { overwrite?: boolean }): Promise<void>
  remove(path: string): Promise<void>
  pathExists(path: string): Promise<boolean>
  pathExistsSync(path: string): boolean
  ensureDir(path: string, options?: { mode?: number }): Promise<void>
  emptyDir(path: string): Promise<void>
}

/**
 * Shape of server/libs/fsExtra.
 * The vendored fs-extra builds its fs API at runtime (promisified graceful-fs), so the type TypeScript infers
 * from the JS lacks most fs methods. Files cast the required module to this type.
 */
export type FsExtra = typeof fsPromises & Omit<typeof fsSync, keyof typeof fsPromises> & FsExtraMethods

/**
 * Values the server stores on `global` (set in Server.js, Database.js and index.js)
 */
type ServerSettingsJson = ReturnType<ServerSettingsModel['toJSON']>

  var isWin: boolean

  var MetadataPath: string

    const user = this.cache.get(id)

  }

    return user
  }

  getByUsername(username) {
    const user = this.cache.find((u) => u.username === username)
    return user
  }

  getByOldId(oldUserId) {
    const user = this.cache.find((u) => u.extraData?.oldUserId === oldUserId)
    return user
  }

  getByOpenIDSub(sub) {
    const user = this.cache.find((u) => u.extraData?.authOpenIDSub === sub)
    return user
  }

  set(user) {
    user.fromCache = true
    this.cache.set(user.id, user)
  }

  delete(userId) {
    this.cache.delete(userId)
  }

  maybeInvalidate(user) {
    if (!user.fromCache) this.delete(user.id)
  }

729	   */
730	  async createUpdateMediaProgressFromPayload(progressPayload) {
731	    /** @type {import('./MediaProgress')|null} */
732	    let mediaProgress = null
733	    let mediaItemId = null
734	    let podcastId = null
735	    if (progressPayload.episodeId) {
736	      const podcastEpisode = await this.sequelize.models.podcastEpisode.findByPk(progressPayload.episodeId, {
737	        attributes: ['id', 'podcastId'],
738	        include: [
739	          {
740	            model: this.sequelize.models.mediaProgress,
741	            where: { userId: this.id },
742	            required: false
743	          },
744	          {
745	            model: this.sequelize.models.podcast,
746	            attributes: ['id', 'title'],
747	            include: {
748	              model: this.sequelize.models.libraryItem,
749	              attributes: ['id']
750	            }
751	          }
752	        ]
753	      })
754	      if (!podcastEpisode) {
755	        Logger.error(`[User] createUpdateMediaProgress: episode ${progressPayload.episodeId} not found`)
756	        return {
757	          error: 'Episode not found',
758	          statusCode: 404
759	        }
760	      }
761	      mediaItemId = podcastEpisode.id
762	      mediaProgress = podcastEpisode.mediaProgresses?.[0]
763	      podcastId = podcastEpisode.podcastId
764	    } else {
765	      const libraryItem = await this.sequelize.models.libraryItem.findByPk(progressPayload.libraryItemId, {
766	        attributes: ['id', 'mediaId', 'mediaType'],
767	        include: {
768	          model: this.sequelize.models.book,
769	          attributes: ['id', 'title'],
770	          required: false,
771	          include: {
772	            model: this.sequelize.models.mediaProgress,
773	            where: { userId: this.id },
774	            required: false
775	          }
776	        }
777	      })
778	      if (!libraryItem) {
779	        Logger.error(`[User] createUpdateMediaProgress: library item ${progressPayload.libraryItemId} not found`)
780	        return {
781	          error: 'Library item not found',
782	          statusCode: 404
783	        }
784	      } else if (libraryItem.mediaType !== 'book') {
785	        Logger.error(`[User] createUpdateMediaProgress: library item ${progressPayload.libraryItemId} is not a book`)
786	        return {
787	          error: 'Library item is not a book',
788	          statusCode: 400
789	        }
790	      }
791	
792	      mediaItemId = libraryItem.media.id
793	      mediaProgress = libraryItem.media.mediaProgresses?.[0]
794	    }
795	
796	    if (mediaProgress) {
797	      mediaProgress = await mediaProgress.applyProgressUpdate(progressPayload)
798	      this.mediaProgresses = this.mediaProgresses.map((mp) => (mp.id === mediaProgress.id ? mediaProgress : mp))
799	    } else {
800	      const newMediaProgressPayload = {
801	        userId: this.id,
802	        mediaItemId,
803	        podcastId,
804	        mediaItemType: progressPayload.episodeId ? 'podcastEpisode' : 'book',
805	        duration: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.duration) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.duration),
806	        currentTime: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.currentTime) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.currentTime),
807	        isFinished: !!progressPayload.isFinished,
808	        hideFromContinueListening: !!progressPayload.hideFromContinueListening,
809	        ebookLocation: progressPayload.ebookLocation || null,
810	        ebookProgress: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.ebookProgress) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.ebookProgress),
811	        finishedAt: progressPayload.finishedAt || null,
812	        createdAt: progressPayload.createdAt || new Date(),
813	        extraData: {
814	          libraryItemId: progressPayload.libraryItemId,
815	          progress: isNullOrNaN(progressPayload.progress) ? 0 : Number(progressPayload.progress)
816	        }
817	      }
818	      if (newMediaProgressPayload.isFinished) {
819	        newMediaProgressPayload.finishedAt = newMediaProgressPayload.finishedAt || new Date()
820	        newMediaProgressPayload.extraData.progress = 1
821	      } else {
822	        newMediaProgressPayload.finishedAt = null
823	      }
824	      mediaProgress = await this.sequelize.models.mediaProgress.create(newMediaProgressPayload)
825	      this.mediaProgresses.push(mediaProgress)
826	    }
827	    userCache.maybeInvalidate(this)
828	    return {
829	      mediaProgress
830	    }
831	  }

947	  /**
948	   * Update user permissions from external JSON
949	   *
950	   * @param {Object} absPermissions JSON containing user permissions
951	   * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if updates were made
952	   */
953	  async updatePermissionsFromExternalJSON(absPermissions) {
954	    if (!this.permissions) this.permissions = {}
955	    let hasUpdates = false
956	
957	    // Map the boolean permissions from absPermissions
958	    Object.keys(absPermissions).forEach((absKey) => {
959	      const userPermKey = User.permissionMapping[absKey]
960	      if (!userPermKey) {
961	        throw new Error(`Unexpected permission property: ${absKey}`)
962	      }
963	
964	      if (!['librariesAccessible', 'itemTagsSelected'].includes(userPermKey)) {
965	        if (this.permissions[userPermKey] !== !!absPermissions[absKey]) {
966	          this.permissions[userPermKey] = !!absPermissions[absKey]
967	          hasUpdates = true
968	        }
969	      }
970	    })
971	
972	    // Handle allowedLibraries
973	    const librariesAccessible = this.permissions.librariesAccessible || []
974	    if (this.permissions.accessAllLibraries) {
975	      if (librariesAccessible.length) {
976	        this.permissions.librariesAccessible = []
977	        hasUpdates = true
978	      }
979	    } else if (absPermissions.allowedLibraries?.length && absPermissions.allowedLibraries.join(',') !== librariesAccessible.join(',')) {
980	      if (absPermissions.allowedLibraries.some((lid) => typeof lid !== 'string')) {
981	        throw new Error('Invalid permission property "allowedLibraries", expecting array of strings')
982	      }

content.content:
- `git diff --name-status 7d10b8fc HEAD -- tsconfig.server.json eslint.config.mjs test/` prints nothing, and `git status --porcelain` is empty, so the three are unchanged in both HEAD and the working tree. `test/` holds 35 files at both commits.
- `tsconfig.server.json` has `"strict": true`. It also has `allowJs: true` without `checkJs`, so the still-JS modules (models, managers, Database) are not checked and their inferred types are what forces many casts.
- `eslint.config.mjs` only lists `index.js`, `prod.js`, `dev.js`, `server/**/*.js` and `test/**/*.js`, so the 0 eslint-disable count is trivially true: `.ts` files are never linted.

## Cast reasons

Classification of all 443 cast sites. A script (`classify.js`) buckets each cast by its target type and expression; I then read every `as unknown as` (109) and the "drops null" bucket by hand. Bucket sizes are [measured] for the script's rules; the a/b/c/d labels are [judgement].

| Reason | Cast sites | of which `as unknown as` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| (b) Sequelize: `TypedDatabase` views, query option objects, loaded rows with associations, JSON columns, `LibraryItem['media']` | 176 | 52 |
| (b) Express/passport: `req.query`, `req.session`, `express()`, `req.user` | 7 | 2 |
| (a) Vendored or untyped library module (`FsExtra` 13, `DateAndTime` 4, `ArchiverFactory` 2, Fuse, ffprobe, libarchive, fast-sort) | 30 | 22 |
| (a) Loosely typed third-party output (xml2js trees, openid-client, axios errors, provider JSON) | 34 | 1 |
| (c?) Drops `null`/`undefined` or retypes a primitive without a check | 112 | 5 |
| (c) Model JSDoc says a different type than the runtime value (`bigint`, `Date`, `publishedYear`) | 6 | 6 |
| `null as unknown as T` field/variable initialisers | 8 | 8 |
| (d) Dynamic key access (`this as unknown as Record<string, unknown>`, `keyof X`) | 43 | 12 |
| (d) `catch (error)` read as `Error` | 21 | 0 |
| (d) Other | 6 | 1 |
| **Total** | **443** | **109** |

The 109 `as unknown as` by reason [judgement after reading each one]: (a) 23, (b) 52, (c) 18, (d) 16.
- (c), 18: the 8 `null as unknown as T` initialisers; the 6 model-JSDoc mismatches (`absMetadataMigration.ts:53,55,59`, `libraryFilters.ts:154,173,692`); `BookFinder.ts:609` (options passed as isbn, has a NOTE); `Backup.ts:55` (old backups stored `1` in a string field); `dbMigration.ts:1612` (`oldLibraryId` does not exist, has a NOTE); `ApiRouter.ts:621` (sessions read with a string `timeListening` and a missing `lastUpdate`, has a NOTE).
- (d), 16: the 12 `this`-as-Record aliases in objects/*; 3 `isNaN(x as unknown as number)` coercions (`parseOpfMetadata.ts:119`, `podcastUtils.ts:379`, `scandir.ts:219`); `libraryFilters.ts:718` (an object whose Sets are swapped for arrays in place).

Inside the 112 "drops null" bucket [judgement]:
- About 40 are harmless: `process.env.X as string` into `parseInt` (`TokenManager.ts:47-57`, `rateLimiterFactory.ts:36-48`); `arr.pop() as string` / `shift() as string` after a length check (`scandir.ts:84,116`, `parseOverdriveMediaMarkers.ts:156-165`); `isNaN(x as number)`; `clearInterval(this.loop as NodeJS.Timeout)` (`Stream.ts:252` and 4 more).
- About 70 assert that a nullable value is set because the surrounding logic makes it so (`libraryItemsBookFilters.ts:292-315`, `ApiRouter.ts:599,605`, `fileUtils.ts:205,239,241`). These are honest about the JS but give no protection. A few hide real risk (see the top 10).

## Top 10 worst shortcuts

All [judgement], ranked by how much checking each one removes.

1. `server/routers/ApiRouter.ts:61-66,127`: `RouteHandler = (req: never, res: never, next: never) => unknown` and `express() as unknown as ApiRouterApp`. Any function fits a `never`-parameter handler, so none of the 203 `this.router.get/post/patch/delete(...)` registrations is checked (wrong controller, wrong arity, a non-function would all compile).
2. `server/utils/queries/types.ts:66-78` (`QueryFindOptions` with `where`, `include`, `attributes`, `order` all `unknown`) plus `as unknown as FindOptions/CountOptions/FindAndCountOptions` at 27 sites (for example `libraryItemsBookFilters.ts:441,450,461`, `libraryItemsPodcastFilters.ts:141,149,159`). Every Sequelize query built in utils/queries is unchecked.
3. `server/utils/queries/types.ts:43-49`: `FilteredLibraryItem = LibraryItem & { ...; [key: string]: unknown }`. The index signature lets any misspelled property on a library item compile (it reads as `unknown` instead of an error). It is cast to at 8 sites and used in all the filter queries.
4. `x as unknown as LibraryItem['media']` 12 times (for example `libraryItemsBookFilters.ts:768,916,1107,1163,1262,1360`, `libraryItemFilters.ts:60,83,123,146,187`). A Book/Podcast row with its own associations is forced into the model's `media` type. The shapes really differ, and the next line (`libraryItemsBookFilters.ts:1362,1364`) needs yet another cast to `BookExpanded`.

/**
 * Chapter stored in the chapters JSON column""")
open(p,'w').write(s)

    s=open(p).read()
    mod = 'Sequelize' if f=='ApiKey.ts' else 'sequelize'
    start=s.index('  // Same overloads as Model.update')
    end=s.index('  async save(')
    cache='apiKeyCache' if f=='ApiKey.ts' else 'userCache'
    new=f"""  // Same overloads as Model.update
  update<K extends keyof {attrs}>(key: K, value: {attrs}[K] | Utils.Col | Utils.Fn | Utils.Literal, options?: InstanceUpdateOptions<{attrs}>): Promise<this>
  update(keys: UpdateValues<{attrs}>, options?: InstanceUpdateOptions<{attrs}>): Promise<this>
  async update(values: keyof {attrs} | UpdateValues<{attrs}>, options?: InstanceUpdateOptions<{attrs}> | {attrs}[keyof {attrs}] | Utils.Col | Utils.Fn | Utils.Literal): Promise<this> {{
    {cache}.maybeInvalidate(this)
    // cast(b): the two arguments are forwarded as they came (a third update(key, value, options) argument is dropped, as in the JS); the overloads above type the callers
    return await super.update(values as UpdateValues<{attrs}>, options as InstanceUpdateOptions<{attrs}>)
  }}

"""

        if anchor in l:

    count = 0
    for j in range(idx, len(lines)):

    opener = lines[j].rstrip()[-1]

    depth = 0
    for k in range(j, len(lines)):

    close_line = lines[k]

    rest = close_line.strip()[1:]
    lines[k] = ' ' * indent + closer + ' as unknown as ' + target + rest

- server/routers/ApiRouter.ts `getUserListeningStatsHelpers`: reads `s.lastUpdate`, but PlaybackSession has no `lastUpdate` (it is `updatedAt`), so `items[id].lastUpdate` is always undefined.

+- server/models/Collection.ts `getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded`: the permission-filtered books are assigned to `this.books`, which in this static method is the Collection class, not the collection `c`; `c.toOldJSONExpanded()` then uses the unfiltered `c.books`, so users with tag or explicit-content restrictions get every book of a collection they can see (and the class gets a stray `books` property).
+- server/models/Library.ts `getMaxDisplayOrder`: `this.max('displayOrder') || 0` applies `|| 0` to the promise, which is always truthy, so with no libraries it resolves to null instead of 0.
+- server/models/Author.ts `getAllLibraryItemsForAuthor`: `author.books` is read without checking that `findByPk` found the author, so an unknown author id throws a TypeError.

+- server/models/Feed.ts `updateFeedForEntity`: when the library item, collection or series of the feed no longer exists, `getExpandedById` returns null and `getFeedObjFor...` throws a TypeError before the try block (3 places), so the caller gets an exception instead of null.

+- server/models/Playlist.ts `checkHasMediaItem`: without an episodeId it reads `pmi.mediaItem.libraryItem.id` for every item, but a podcast episode media item has no `libraryItem` (it is on `episode.podcast`), so it throws a TypeError for playlists that contain episodes.

+- server/models/PodcastEpisode.ts `createFromRssPodcastEpisode`: RSS chapters can have `end: null` (the RSS parser types them so), and they are stored in the `chapters` column, which everything else reads as chapters with a numeric end.
+- server/models/LibraryItem.ts `saveMetadataFile`: the podcast branch writes `asin: mediaExpanded.asin`, but Podcast has no asin, so it is always undefined (and left out of metadata.json).

+- server/models/User.ts `checkCanAccessLibraryItem`: `libraryItem.media.metadata?.explicit` reads a property of the old models; Book and Podcast have no `metadata`, so that half of the explicit check is always false.

+- server/models/Session.ts `refreshToken` (with server/auth/TokenManager.ts `createTokensAndSession`, `rotateTokensForSession`): the column is NOT NULL, but TokenManager writes `generateRefreshToken` results, which are null when signing fails; the create/update then fails validation and throws instead of reporting the signing error.
### Batch 1: server/utils (46 files, all converted, none skipped)
- Non-null assertions (`!`, each with a comment): `FileMetadata.filenameNoExt`, OidcAuthStrategy `handleMobileRedirect` (`openIdAuthSession.get(state)!`, `has(state)` is checked just before).
- Result: `npm run build:server` reports 0 `error TS`; `npm test` 356 passing, 0 failing.
+### Batch 3a: server/models (25 files, all converted, none skipped)
+- File count: 25 `.js` files under server/models (no subfolders), as the Progress table says. New type file: `server/models/types.ts` (JSON column shapes, the model registry, `UpdateValues`).
+- devDependencies added (rule 10): `@types/jsonwebtoken` (ApiKey requires the npm `jsonwebtoken` package, which has no types; TokenManager uses the vendored libs/jsonwebtoken).

+  - Every model is `Model<InferAttributes<X>, InferCreationAttributes<X>>` with all columns as `declare` fields (rule 12), so Sequelize's attribute getters are not shadowed and the classes compile without fields. `CreationOptional` marks columns with a default or that callers may leave out; `NonAttribute` marks associations, expanded properties and getters.

+  - JSON columns are typed in types.ts: `UserPermissions` (keys optional because older users may lack some), `UserExtraData`, `AudioBookmarkObject`, `LibraryFileObject`, `LibrarySettingsObject`, `LibraryExtraData`, `LibraryItemExtraData`, `PodcastEpisodeExtraData`, `MediaProgressExtraData`, `PlaybackSessionExtraData`, `DeviceExtraData`, `AudioFileObject`, `EBookFileObject`, `ChapterObject`; `PlaybackSession.mediaMetadata` uses `PlaybackMediaMetadata` from utils/types.ts; `ApiKey.permissions` is `ApiKeyPermissions` (all keys required, as its JSDoc); `Setting.value` is the constructor input of the email, server or notification settings with its id.

+  - Associations are declared on both sides where the code reads them (`book.libraryItem`, `book.authors`, `book.series`, `book.mediaProgresses`, `series.bookSeries`, `series.books`, `author.books`, `podcast.podcastEpisodes`, `podcast.libraryItem`, `podcastEpisode.podcast`, `podcastEpisode.mediaProgresses`, `libraryItem.media`/`book`/`podcast`, `playlist.playlistMediaItems`, `playlistMediaItem.playlist`/`mediaItem`/`book`/`podcastEpisode`, `feed.feedEpisodes`/`entity`/..., `collection.books`/`feeds`, `session.user`, `apiKey.user`/`createdByUser`, `device.user`, `mediaProgress.mediaItem`/`book`/`podcastEpisode`/`user`, ...) plus the association mixins the code calls (`getBook`, `getPodcast`, `getBooks`, `getFeeds`, `getPlaylistMediaItems`, ...). Expanded properties that the JSDoc typed as always set (`book.authors`, `book.series`, `libraryItem.media`, `podcast.podcastEpisodes`, `feed.feedEpisodes`, `user.mediaProgresses`, ...) stay non-optional; the others are optional. `book.libraryItem` and `podcast.libraryItem` are optional (the earlier batches already delete them), with `Book.BookExpandedWithLibraryItem` / `Podcast.PodcastExpandedWithLibraryItem` for rows loaded with them (collections, series, authors, playlists).

+  - `LibraryItem.LibraryItemExpanded` is a union of `BookLibraryItem` (`mediaType: 'book'`, `media: Book`) and `PodcastLibraryItem`, so code that checks `mediaType` on an expanded item gets the right media without a cast (Feed, FeedEpisode). `getExpandedById`, `findOneExpanded` and `findAllExpandedWhere` return it.

+  - `size`, `mtime`, `ctime` as they are at runtime: `LibraryItem.size` is a `number` (BIGINT, which sqlite returns as a number; the JSDoc said BigInt). `mtime`, `ctime` and `birthtime` are read as `Date | null` but are also set to epoch ms (file timestamps), which the DATE(6) columns convert to Dates; they are declared as accessor pairs in an interface merged with the class (get `Date | null`, set `Date | number | null`) and the creation attributes accept numbers. The same pattern is used for `PodcastEpisode.publishedAt`, `MediaProgress.finishedAt` (also date strings) and `Podcast.lastEpisodeCheck`, and the creation attributes of `PlaybackSession` accept epoch ms for `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. `FeedEpisode.enclosureSize` is a `number` and `PodcastEpisode.enclosureSize` is `number | string | null` (a new episode keeps the RSS length string until reloaded); both JSDocs said BigInt.

+  - Null (rule 15): columns the models assign null to or create with null are `T | null` (for example the book and podcast string metadata, which `updateFromRequest` sets to null, `BookSeries.sequence`, `ebookFile`, `finishedAt`). `Library.settings` and `Podcast.numEpisodes` keep the JSDoc type (not null): the model only uses `||` as a fallback in one getter and never writes null, while all other code reads them directly. `Session.refreshToken` is `string | null` because TokenManager writes nullable tokens (see Bugs).

No cast is needed, and `this.findAll(...)` etc. are typed inside the models.

+  - `sequelize.models` is typed through `ModelsSequelize` (`Sequelize & { models: ModelRegistry; uppercaseFirst }`, where `uppercaseFirst` is added by Database.init). Models that use it declare `declare sequelize: ModelsSequelize` and/or `declare static readonly sequelize: ModelsSequelize` (compiles to nothing), so `this.sequelize.models.feedEpisode.createFromBooks(...)` needs no cast.

Batch 3a is finished and committed as `e31a29ec phase3 batch 3a: models`. The build reports 0 `error TS` (after a clean rebuild) and `npm test` shows 356 passing, 0 failing. No test was edited, skipped or deleted, and I did not start 3b.

**Scope.** The real count matches the prompt: 25 `.js` files under `server/models`, with no subfolders. All 25 are converted and none were skipped. There is one new file, `server/models/types.ts`, for the shared JSON-column types. I added `@types/jsonwebtoken` as a devDependency because ApiKey uses the npm `jsonwebtoken` package, which has no types.

**Rule 13 (what batch 3b needs):**
- **JSON columns are typed:** `permissions`, `extraData` (one type per model), `mediaMetadata`, `libraryFiles`, `settings`, `bookmarks`, `audioFiles`, `chapters` and the rest.
- **Associations are declared,** e.g. `book.libraryItem`, `series.bookSeries`, `libraryItem.media`, `feed.feedEpisodes`, plus the association getters the code calls.
- **`LibraryItem.LibraryItemExpanded`** is now a book-or-podcast union, so checking `mediaType` gives the right `media` type without a cast.
- **`size`** is a `number`, which is what sqlite returns; the old JSDoc said BigInt.
- **`mtime`, `ctime`, `birthtime`** read as `Date | null`, but can also be set to epoch milliseconds, which is what the code does at runtime.
- **Static method calls now type-check.** The models' `init(sequelize)` overrides were why TypeScript rejected `findAll`, `count` and the other static methods. Each model now declares two `init` signatures, with no cast, so those calls are typed inside the models. `sequelize.models.*` is typed as well.
- `TypedDatabase`, `ApiDatabase`, `PatchModels` and `QueryFindOptions` are left in place.

**Behaviour.** I compared the compiled JS of all 25 models and the 8 edited non-model files against HEAD. The only differences are the ones listed in the Log: the removed constructors (they only read properties), the import style, and local aliases. I also started the server against an empty config and checked init, login, a wrong-password login, the library list and creating a library; all behaved normally.
- **One argument was removed.** `getMediaItemsInProgress(..., limit, false)` is now called without the `false`. The function has always taken only 4 parameters, so that argument was ignored, but TypeScript rejects it. There is a comment at the line and an entry in the Log.

**Edits outside `server/models`.** The stricter model types broke the build in 8 files. Each fix is type-only and listed in the Log with the old and new expression:
- `OidcAuthStrategy.ts`: 2 casts.
- `AudioTrack.ts`: `setFromStream` now accepts a null title.
- `absMetadataMigration.ts`: the old `as unknown as bigint` cast is removed.
- `dbMigration.ts`: 7 casts on `bulkCreate` calls that pass partial rows, and 2 on titles.
- `authorFilters.ts` and the other query files: computed attributes added to the local row types, plus 2 casts.

**Bugs found (listed, not fixed), 9 new:**
- **Collection:** the permission filter in `getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded` assigns the filtered books to the class instead of the collection. Users with tag or explicit-content restrictions therefore see all books of a collection they can see.
- **Library:** in `getMaxDisplayOrder`, the `|| 0` applies to the promise, so an empty table gives null instead of 0.
- **Author:** `getAllLibraryItemsForAuthor` throws for an unknown author id.
- **Feed:** `updateFeedForEntity` throws when the item, collection or series behind the feed no longer exists (3 places).
- **Playlist:** `checkHasMediaItem` throws for playlists that contain podcast episodes.
- **PodcastEpisode:** chapters from RSS feeds can be stored with `end: null`, though everything else expects a number.
- **LibraryItem:** the podcast metadata file reads `asin`, which podcasts don't have.
- **User:** `checkCanAccessLibraryItem` reads `media.metadata`, which no longer exists, so that half of the explicit check is always false.
- **Session:** `refreshToken` is a NOT NULL column, but TokenManager can write null when token signing fails, so the save throws.

**Rule 17 counts (whole batch):**

| | Count |
|---|---|
| `as` | 58 |
| `as unknown as` | 27 |
| non-null `!` | 9 |
| tag a | 2 |
| tag b | 33 |
| tag c | 5 (each has a NOTE and a Bugs entry) |
| tag d | 45 |

No single kind of cast goes over 10. The largest groups are narrowing `media` by `mediaType` (8) and the `bulkCreate` partial-row casts (7). Counting all `as number` casts together gives 11. I split them by reason (Date subtraction, `isNaN`/undefined, the `limit`/`offset` arguments), and none of those groups is over 10.

**Judgement calls:**
- **Kept non-null:** `Library.settings` and `Podcast.numEpisodes` stay non-null, as the JSDoc had them. The model only uses `||` as a fallback in one getter, and making them nullable would have needed non-null assertions in five query files.
- **Made nullable:** `Session.refreshToken` is `string | null`, matching how TokenManager already uses it.

In git, 10 of the smaller renamed files show as delete plus add rather than a rename. They were moved with `git mv`, but removing the constructors changed most of their lines, so git no longer recognises them as renames.
